svg.title: LinkedIn Activity and Response Checkpoints
svg.desc: diagram id: diag-02-linkedin-acquisition-checkpoints; chapter number: 6; title: LinkedIn Activity and Response Checkpoints; subtitle: Keep sent counts, acceptance rates, message counts, response rates, and advertising engagement distinct.; caption: Jack reports workspace connection and messaging results; Adam Holmgren separately gives a cold thought-leader advertising engagement benchmark.; assumptions note: Jack's counts and percentages are different measures, not five comparable cohort counts. Adam Holmgren's benchmark belongs to a separate advertising approach. Numeric widths must not imply a continuous conversion funnel or comparable magnitude across these mixed units.; note: Jack — 4RYnbUHayhM at 00:01:24, 00:02:18, and 00:02:32; Adam Holmgren — qy4FW_qglNo at 00:06:20. No accepted-contact count, reply count, or sales count is inferred.; chart type: funnel; stages: label: Connection requests sent; value: 31000; display: About 31,000 requests; conversion: Activity count, not a conversion rate; detail: Jack describes the previous year's connection requests in the displayed workspace.; label: Connection acceptance rate; value: 34; display: 34% accepted; conversion: Reported request acceptance rate; detail: Jack reports the percentage accepted; an accepted contact count is not supplied.; label: Messages sent; value: 10000; display: Close to 10,000 messages; conversion: No acceptance-to-message rate supplied; detail: Jack reports message volume separately from connection acceptance.; label: Message response rate; value: 26; display: About 26% responses; conversion: Reported message response rate; detail: Jack reports responses, not qualified meetings or completed sales.; label: Cold advertising engagement; value: 15; display: Above 15% engagement-inclusive CTR; conversion: Separate advertising benchmark; detail: Adam Holmgren calls above 15% good for cold thought-leader advertising. This CTR includes likes and see-more clicks, not only site visits.

circle.title: label: Connection requests sent; value: 31000; display: About 31,000 requests; conversion: Activity count, not a conversion rate; detail: Jack describes the previous year's connection requests in the displayed workspace.

label: Connection acceptance rate; value: 34; display: 34% accepted; conversion: Reported request acceptance rate; detail: Jack reports the percentage accepted; an accepted contact count is not supplied.
label: Messages sent; value: 10000; display: Close to 10,000 messages; conversion: No acceptance-to-message rate supplied; detail: Jack reports message volume separately from connection acceptance.
label: Message response rate; value: 26; display: About 26% responses; conversion: Reported message response rate; detail: Jack reports responses, not qualified meetings or completed sales.

label: Cold advertising engagement; value: 15; display: Above 15% engagement-inclusive CTR; conversion: Separate advertising benchmark; detail: Adam Holmgren calls above 15% good for cold thought-leader advertising. This CTR includes likes and see-more clicks, not only site visits.

text.title: Assumptions: Jack's counts and percentages are different measures, not five comparable cohort counts. Adam Holmgren's benchmark belongs to a separate advertising approach. Numeric widths must not imply a continuous conversion funnel or comparable magnitude across these mixed units.
